body:
Triage: queued as Bug — a `field:`-prefixed `password` / `email` field falling back to `type="text"` renders a secret in clear text; user-reachable on any app whose widget registration is incomplete, fix lands in the fields fallback path (the unregistered-widget default must respect the declared input type, or refuse to render the value rather than degrade to clear text). Fail-closed direction note for the claimer: for `password` specifically, prefer masking/refusal over best-effort rendering — a silent degrade to clear text is the exact tolerance-hides-errors shape the platform rejects. Size/model suggestion: S–M.

Serial constraints cleared: `packages/fields` was held by #5214 through round 18; **PR5369 merged as `5458414a7`**, so it is free. `packages/components/src/renderers/form/form.tsx` has no in-flight claim — #5253 (same branch, ceiling defect) is closed, #5254's PR5326 is merged. Round-19 siblings hold disjoint surfaces (#5342 `scripts/check-doc-component-types.mjs`; #5081 `skills/objectui/guides/i18n.md`).

**Direction is set by triage — ⛔ do not re-open the A/B the card left open.** Triage graded this Bug and ruled on it (comment 5344110871), verbatim: *"the unregistered-widget default must respect the declared input type, or refuse to render the value rather than degrade to clear text"*, with a **fail-closed direction note**: *"for `password` specifically, prefer masking/refusal over best-effort rendering — a silent degrade to clear text is the exact tolerance-hides-errors shape the platform rejects."*

So the card's option A (normalize the table key) is acceptable **only** where it fails closed. For `password` the bar is higher than "render it as a password box": a `field:`-prefixed type that resolves nothing means the app shipped without the widget it declares, and the value must not appear in clear text under any branch. Choose the shape that satisfies both halves of the ruling and say which you chose and why.

## What is measured and what is not

Measured and reproduced by the filer:
```
get(field:password) = false
rendered type = text
attrs = ["class","id","aria-describedby","aria-invalid","type","name"]
```
The default branch reads `inputType`, which an object-derived field does not carry. `mapFieldTypeToFormType` emits the `field:`-prefixed id for **every** object-derived form, so this is the normal path, not an edge case.

⚠️ **Pre-existing, and not caused by #5254.** Verified against `origin/main` before that change as well. `NATIVE_INPUT_FIELD_TYPES` is keyed on the raw `type`, so the prefixed spelling misses it. ⛔ Do not describe this as a #5254 regression in the PR.

Re-measure at your branch point — `main` has moved (`f2e11ae6f` at time of writing) and PR5326's table is what you are extending.

## Verification

- Pin the **rendered output**, not the resolver: assert what a `field:password` renders as, for the unregistered-widget case. The whole defect is that the resolver returning nothing still produced a plausible-looking control.
- Reverse-verify: revert your change and show the pin goes red with `type="text"` in the failure text.
- Cover **both** spellings (`password` and `field:password`) and both types (`password`, `email`) — the bare spellings must keep the behaviour PR5326 gave them. A fix that trades one spelling for the other is not a fix.
- **Run tests from the repo root, not `pnpm --filter <pkg> test`** — 17 packages own a standalone `vitest.config.ts` that does not re-export the root config, so a package-scoped run uses a different config than CI does.
- State per leg whether a build artifact sits between your edit and the thing under test.

Changeset: `patch`. ⛔ **Never `major`** (maintainer 2026-08-19: 「objectui ui 的 major 是要跟着 objectstack 走的,不可以自己发 major」). ⛔ Do not touch `content/docs/releases/`.

Draft PR, `Fixes #5322`.

## What I verified at source rather than taking from the PR body

The shape is a judgment call — the dev used **both** limbs of the triage ruling, one per spelling — so I checked the branch itself rather than the prose describing it.

`form.tsx:3424`: `if (type.startsWith('field:') && SECRET_FIELD_TYPES.has(declaredType))`. **Both conjuncts.** So the refusal cannot reach a bare `password`, which falls through to `NATIVE_INPUT_FIELD_TYPES[declaredType]` at `:3489` and keeps `type="password"`. `inputType ||` still takes precedence there, so an explicit `inputType` is untouched. The PR body's table is accurate, and the blast radius is what it claims: `field:currency` / `field:qrcode` still render their text boxes, a registered `field:password` widget still wins, `ui:`-qualified ids are unchanged.

**The reasoning for refusing rather than masking is the part I would have pushed back on if it were thinner, and it is not.** Masking closes the leak and is exactly what the bare spelling does. What makes it insufficient here is the extra fact the prefix carries: reaching that arm with a `field:`-prefixed id *proves* the app shipped without the widget it declares, so a masked box would invite a user to type a secret into a form whose password widget — strength meter, confirm pair, reveal toggle, submit handling — is absent, in a control that looks like it worked. Triage's ruling explicitly offered either limb and said "prefer masking/refusal" for `password`; choosing refusal is inside that grant, not a re-adjudication.

**Reverse verification does what the dispatch asked**: 6 red / 10 green with `form.tsx` reverted, and the seeded-secret leg prints the pre-fix DOM carrying `type="text" value="hunter2"` — the defect in the failure text, not merely an assertion about it. The 10 that stay green are the bare-spelling pins and the no-collateral cases, so the file would also catch a fix that traded one spelling for the other, which was the specific trap the dispatch named.

## ⚠️ This closes a partial fix, and that must not be read as the class being shut

`Fixes #5322` will close this card with a title reading *"a secret shown in clear text"*. **That condition is closed on the producer-reachable path only.** Three spellings still render `type="text"`, filed as **#5375**: `ui:password`, a hand-authored bare `secret`, and `field:secret`. None is emitted by a producer — an object-derived `secret` field is safe because `mapFieldTypeToFormType` maps it to `field:password`, which this PR answers — so they are reachable only from a hand-authored standalone form, which is genuinely lower severity.

The detail worth carrying: **`ui:password` *is* registered**, as an SDUI node renderer. So an author who checks whether it resolves gets a *yes*, and still gets a clear-text box on the field path. Verifying does not protect you there.

Leaving the two of them (`field:` half fixed, three spellings open) linked in both directions rather than letting a closed card imply more than it delivered.
